notes: This minor release adds four native Go standard-library packs, tightens when 25 Go packs activate, and makes nine TypeScript and Node packs active by default. It is built by the same released, checksum-pinned bifrost-semantic-pack 0.15.1 as packs 0.10.0 (public commit 04fdd17d2606d13a7a5f13b012bfbe3ad9729d1e, executable SHA-256 7322cdbd653830aaba349c9a278eceb97573965739b2845412a3074080b6acc2), so it still needs Bifrost 0.15.1 or later and the bundle keeps release index schema 4 and the same semantic-model read schemas (8, 14, 16, 19, 22) and lists 68 packs. New native packs: bifrost.go.stdlib.io-declarations 1.0.0 (22 exported interfaces, 14 declared interface methods, and the io.ReadAll, io.Copy and io.LimitReader functions; partial) (#244); bifrost.go.stdlib.io 0.1.0 (complete summaries for io.ReadAll and io.LimitReader; io.Copy has no summary because the semantic-model schema cannot express its write into the destination); and bifrost.go.stdlib.compress-gzip-declarations and bifrost.go.stdlib.compress-gzip 0.2.0 (gzip.NewReader summaries) (#320). All four are BSD-3-Clause and derived from Go 1.26.0. Incompatible change, with migration: the 25 Go standard-library packs other than bifrost.go.stdlib.io now declare the Go toolchain range >=1.26.0, <2.0.0 as both compatibility and activation selector (#328), because the exact-coordinate activation gate cannot bind a pack with an empty selector. They are no longer selected on a project whose Go toolchain is older than 1.26.0 or whose version Bifrost cannot read, where they were previously selected without any version check; those projects get a version near-miss warning and no Go standard-library models. The 21 packs that were in packs 0.10.0 move to 3.0.0 (bytes, crypto/x509, encoding/pem, errors, log, net, net/http, net/url, os, path/filepath, sync/atomic and testing, in declaration and summary pairs where both exist), and bifrost.go.stdlib.encoding-gob and its declarations pack move from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0. Bifrost 0.15.1 reads these selectors (dependency-pack activation compares the discovered Go toolchain version with the pack's toolchain selector), so no newer engine is required. To migrate, build with Go 1.26.0 or later. bifrost.go.stdlib.io 0.1.0 still has an empty selector. Also changed: bifrost.python-stdlib-api-declarations 0.6.0 adds the webbrowser module with open, open_new and open_new_tab, and bifrost.python-security-sink-summaries 0.5.0 adds a summary for each (#323). Nine packs keep their version and identity but are no longer review-required, so they now activate without an entry in .bifrost/packs.json (#327): bifrost.typescript-stdlib 7.0.2, bifrost.node-buffer-javascript-declarations and bifrost.node-buffer-typescript-declarations 0.1.0, bifrost.node-child-process-javascript-declarations and bifrost.node-child-process-typescript-declarations 0.2.0, bifrost.node-child-process-javascript-summaries and bifrost.node-child-process-typescript-summaries 0.1.0, and bifrost.node-runtime-values-javascript and bifrost.node-runtime-values-typescript 0.1.0. Their model content and measurement record counts are unchanged, but findings that depend on them can now appear by default. bifrost.rust-stdlib stays review-required (see AGENTS.md). Source-only or staged, not native additions: the C# models bifrost.dotnet.system-data-csharp and bifrost.dotnet.system-text-regularexpressions-csharp 0.1.0 (#319); the Node path and url models 0.1.0 and bifrost.node-fs-javascript-summaries 0.2.0 (#317); the CodeQL Rust standard-library summaries codeql.rust-stdlib.summaries 1.0.0 (#326); and the Rust std module-function remodel in bifrost.rust-std-sql-taint (#329). None of these is in a release recipe, so no pack was removed. Rules 0.10.0 keeps its exact dependency on packs 0.10.0; rules 0.11.0 moves it here. Generation, integrity, compatibility and per-run completeness remain separate from behavior qualification.
